 Early voting starts Monday for District 3 runoff 
 Early voting starts Monday for the Richmond County Board of Education District 3 runoff. By Kalei Nash Updated : 6 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google AUGUSTA, Ga. (WRDW/WAGT) - Early voting starts Monday for the Richmond County Board of Education District 3 runoff. 
 Voters will choose between Kenyatta Brown and Carol Yancy after neither candidate won enough votes in the midterms. Election Day is Dec. 1.
 CSRA Habitat for Humanity ReStore closes as focus shifts to housing 
 Augusta/CSRA Habitat for Humanity is officially closing a familiar storefront, but not its mission.
 Brown is a nursing professor. Yancy is a former educator. 
 Both are parents, and both would be new members of the board. One seat is open.
 “You always talk about change,” Brown said. “Here I am. I believe that change is an action word. I’m ready to work.”
 “I think I’m uniquely qualified for the position as a parent and as an educator,” Yancy said.
 Voters will see two races for the District 3 seat on the same ballot. 
 One is a special election to serve through December. The other is the regular election for the full term starting in January.
 Voters could choose one candidate in the special election and the other candidate in the regular election.
 Name released for 61-year-old murder victim in Augusta 
 Authorities have identified a man who died after a shooting Sunday. He was shot at least one time and pronounced dead in the 3000 block of Deans Bridge Road.
 Yancy said student achievement, safety and teacher support are priorities. 
 Before making changes, she said she wants to review what is already in place.
 “What I would really want to do is to look at all the policies and make sure that policy efficacy is good,” Yancy said.
 Brown is campaigning on supporting educators and strengthening community engagement. 
 She said she wants to start by listening.
 “I want to talk to the teachers in particular to see what are their concerns,” Brown said. “Once they voice their concerns, then we can address it.”
